findings: R1 (Flat/CBGCompact, sorry-free): J⁻(p) ∩ Σ compact WITHOUT a limit-curve theorem. B = points x such that for every neighbourhood V, J⁻(V) ∩ Σ lies in no compact set; B is closed and a future set (J⁻ of an open set is open, flat push-up along the chronal flow); frontier step (exists_pastNoncompactAt_frontier): for y ∈ B and compact N ∋ y in its interior, some point of ∂N ∩ J⁻(y) ∩ J⁺(Σ) is in B, so B ∩ Σ = ∅ (Σ acausal); Zorn on CurvesExtend time graphs inside B gives an inextensible causal curve inside B, which must meet Σ: contradiction. Compactness of diamonds is never used; the former SORRY text (limit curves needed) is withdrawn. General model-free form: Causality.isCompact_Jminus_inter_of_isCauchySurface (+ past form via C.dual).

A3 for the flat model (Flat/CBGGerm, sorry-free): the causal localisation of Lemma 3.8 is germ_core (ψ → q along the chart segment κ p − s·ε e₀ ⊆ U); the connected piece is U ∩ κ⁻¹(B(κp,ρ₁) ∩ I^ε(c)) (Sbierski's W ⊆ I⁺(γ(−ε))), not U ∩ B for a chart cylinder; one groupoid element there by B1 rigidity on a star-shaped set. Uses the model's compactness field only to make J^±(Σ) a neighbourhood of p, q (lem:Sigma_separe) — removable via flat_isClosed_Jplus_Jminus_of_isCauchySurface, which CBGGerm cannot import.

A4 for the flat model (Flat/CBGSlice, sorry-free): no slice through p and no hyperboloid. The corner condition puts the punctured past cone of p near p inside U (causal convexity of U); a closed slice ball {t = t(p) − δ, ‖x − x(p)‖ ≤ δ} lies in U, so does an open one of radius ρ > δ; the diamond N over it contains p, its equatorial slice Γ ⊆ U is Cauchy in N, and U' = U ⊔ N is GH with S Cauchy. Uses neither R1 nor GH of U. This also answers the earlier 1+1 B4 caution (B4's piece N is not used). Open for CBG/NoCorresponding (not this package): A4's type does not require U' ∖ U to be reached by A3's extension.

B4 caution (earlier finding, kept for packages 6/11): the Level-B field B4 as approved is satisfied by the flat time ∓t on a small diamond and lacks Sbierski's τ_q localisation; 1+1 counterexample U = {t < −|x|/2}, Σ = {t = −1 − |x|/2}, p = 0, q = (δ,0). Irrelevant to the flat instance now that A4 is proved directly.
B3 curvesExtend holds on every flat spacetime (T2, SC) without global hyperbolicity, via the chronal causal flow (flat_curvesExtend).
B2 localUnique_reg for the flat model uses neither injectivity nor the MapsTo hypothesis (flat_localUnique_reg).
R1 reduction (proved, any causality): tarentin + GH + T2 + J⁺(Σ) closed + J⁻(p) ∩ Σ compact ⇒ J⁺(Σ) ∩ J⁻(p) compact (isCompact_Jplus_inter_Jminus_of_isCompact).

kb_proposals: Level-B structures are Σ' (ChartedSpace, HasGroupoid): a lemma stated with section instances [ChartedSpace Y M] [HasGroupoid M G] does not fire on LocalModel.causality s (the HasGroupoid instance depends on s.1); first `letI := s.1; haveI : HasGroupoid M G := s.2` and `show chartedCausality … M`, then rewrite.

An IsCauchySurfaceOn W S only sees S ∩ W (isCauchySurfaceOn_congr in Flat/CBG); with isCauchySurfaceOn_graph_of_saturated (Flat/LipschitzGraph) for a constant graph, the slice t = c is Cauchy in the Minkowski diamond centred at time c — the cheap local Cauchy slice.
